clue.text: Pilot a plane quite new in style…

definitions.note: a style is the name or title by which someone is known

indicators.note: something made quite new is remade, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Flying a brand-new aircraft with real panache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite new' rearranges PILOT A PLANE; 'style' is the noun meaning a formal title, not flair.
explanation.definitionFit: A style is a formal name or title, which is exactly what this designation word means.

clue.text: Some happy revellers building a bonfire

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few merrymakers are piling up wood for a bonfire.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across haPPY REvellers, with 'Some' marking a portion of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap of wood built up for burning is this, whether for a bonfire or a funeral.

clue.text: Rubbing out-it's time to give voice

parts.note: an era is a period of time
to sing is to give voice in song

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop erasing the board and start singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing out pencil marks is removing them with an eraser.

clue.text: Set down the money first

parts.note: L stands for pounds, the British money (from Latin libra)
first is written 1ST, read as IST

explanation.surface: Someone insists on putting the money on the table before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is written 1st, with the figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something down in writing item by item is to record it in a column.

clue.text: A vessel the French treat with contempt

parts.note: a tramp is a cargo ship with no fixed route
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French people are said to sneer at a certain ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A tramp steamer is a ship that picks up cargo wherever it can.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp on someone's feelings is to treat them with contempt.

clue.text: The ordinary seaman retains a right to fit propellers

indicators.note: retains says the seaman's letters hold the next pieces inside them

explanation.surface: A junior sailor keeps his right to fit the ship's propellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Blades pulled through water to drive a rowing boat are its means of propulsion.

clue.text: Boat poles may be used-poles supplied as part of the service

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words may be used in another order

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Poles from a boat get pressed into use at a formal dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be used' rearranges BOAT POLES into TABLESPOO; the second 'poles' adds N and S, north and south. 'service' is a set of cutlery and crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Large spoons for serving belong to a canteen of cutlery, a dinner service.

clue.text: …there's a place in Kent offering wide-ranging flights

parts.note: broad means wide-ranging
flights of steps are stairs

explanation.surface: A Kent town is said to offer extensive staircases.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues from 1 across's ellipsis; the stray B is a print artefact. Kent is a county in south-east England, and this is a seaside town there.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a seaside resort on the Isle of Thanet in the county of Kent.

clue.text: Fabulous aircraft

parts.note: fabulous in the sense of found in fables: the flying craft of witches in folk tales

explanation.surface: An amazing plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Witches in fairy tales fly on brushes with long handles, a craft of fable.

clue.text: He's on board to deal with complaints

definitions.text: He's on board to deal with complaints

parts.words: He's on board to deal with complaints
parts.note: reads like a company director handling grievances, but means a medic aboard a vessel treating ailments

explanation.surface: A board member handles customer grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical officer serving on a vessel treats complaints in the sense of illnesses.

clue.text: Hunter may well go ahead

definitions.meaning: someone who stalks deer is a hunter
read as 'go a head': a hat with peaks front and back that sits on a head

explanation.surface: A hunter will probably press on.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both one who stalks game and the peaked cap associated with Sherlock Holmes.

clue.text: A civic head about to give ground

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A mayor is about to cede some land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'civic head' looks like a mayor; 'head' instead takes the first letter of 'civic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure of land area, so a piece of ground.

clue.text: A woman keeps nothing that's worn

indicators.note: keeps says the woman's letters hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: she refers to a woman
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A woman holds on to nothing worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is something worn on the foot.

clue.text: Observing a game top man

parts.note: loo is an old card game
a king is the top man in a realm

explanation.surface: Someone watches a game being won by its chief player.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is an old card game, not the British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Observing is watching or regarding something.

clue.text: Colour, being inexperienced

explanation.surface: A shade of a person new to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the shade of grass and also means raw or naive.

clue.text: Pipers, possibly about fifty, going on foot

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the next piece
possibly says the letters may be in a different order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: About fifty pipers are walking along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges PIPERS to SIPPER, and 'about' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft indoor shoe is something that goes on the foot.

clue.text: Fume when meat's found to be bad

indicators.note: meat that has gone bad is spoiled, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone seethes on finding the meat has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Fume as a noun means vapour, such as rises from boiling water.

clue.text: Irritate the old monarch with a note

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
te is a note in sol-fa

explanation.surface: An old king annoys someone by sending a note.
explanation.walkthrough: GR stands for George Rex, as on old British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To grate on someone is to annoy them.

clue.text: A quarter remains for the band

parts.note: S is south, one of the four compass quarters
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A part of the remains is set aside for the musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: A little publicity-it's not way out

parts.note: an ad is a small piece of advertising
the word it, the 's ignored

explanation.surface: A small promotion claims something isn't over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not way out' looks like slang for not extreme; it means an entrance rather than an exit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a horizontal passage into a mine, its entrance rather than its exit.

clue.text: "Hark! from that moonlit what a burst!" (Arnold: Philomela)

definitions.text: "Hark! from that moonlit what a burst!" (Arnold: Philomela)

parts.words: "Hark! from that moonlit what a burst!" (Arnold: Philomela)
parts.note: a quotation with a word missing between moonlit and what: the tree in which the nightingale sings

explanation.surface: A line of Victorian verse about a nightingale.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the missing word from Matthew Arnold's poem about the nightingale.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's nightingale sings from a moonlit evergreen conifer.

clue.text: Study pipe run

parts.note: to con is to study
a duct is a pipe

explanation.surface: A survey of a pipeline route.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct a business is to run or manage it.

clue.text: He will not have scraps on the river

parts.note: refuse is waste, scraps
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A man won't stand for litter on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: One who declines an offer is a person who will not have it.

clue.text: Greek character involved in vegetable assessment

indicators.note: involved in says the Greek letter is wrapped up inside the vegetable

parts.note: an onion is a vegetable
pi is a Greek letter

explanation.surface: A Greek gets mixed up in rating vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or judgment formed about something.

clue.text: Therapeutic, so it may be claimed

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters of the next word could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A treatment is said to be healing.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to healing and treatment of illness, as therapeutic does.

clue.text: Oriental family backing the goddess of victory

indicators.note: backing says the joined pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: E is east, the Orient
kin are family

explanation.surface: An eastern family supports the Greek goddess of victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns E plus KIN round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this winged deity personified triumph.

clue.text: A nymph's city house

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A nymph owns a house in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postal district covering the City, the financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth she was a mountain nymph who faded until only her voice remained.

clue.text: Continental guy raising fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word upward, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A European man grows fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a male first name used in Germany and elsewhere in Europe.

clue.text: Manage ceremonial apparel

definitions.meaning: to get by, deal with something
a long cloak worn by clergy at ceremonies

explanation.surface: Organise the formal robes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to deal with something and also names a priest's semicircular vestment.

clue.text: To resign from choice demands courage

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the following words

explanation.surface: Giving up one's choice takes courage.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across choiCE DEmands.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a claim or territory is to yield it.

clue.text: Cuts are most upsetting for a youth-leader

indicators.note: upsetting knocks the letters of the three words into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Funding cuts most distress a youth club leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of a troop of young people in the Scout movement.

clue.text: Bill holds a peer, means to send cash

indicators.note: holds says the bill's letters contain the next pieces

parts.note: a bill is a poster
a lord is a peer

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill holds a nobleman's money transfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is a printed notice. This is a British money transfer document bought at a post office.
explanation.definitionFit: A document bought at a post office and cashed by the recipient, used to send money.
